name: Network Firewall Configuration
description: Install and maintain network security controls (firewalls, cloud security groups) to protect the cardholder data environment (CDE) from untrusted networks

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 1 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Configuration standards for NSC rulesets are defined, implemented, and maintained
All services, protocols, and ports allowed are identified, approved, and have a defined business need

name: DMZ and Network Segmentation
description: Implement a DMZ and network segmentation to restrict inbound and outbound traffic to only that which is necessary for the cardholder data environment

library_measure_controls.control_name: Inbound traffic to the CDE is restricted to only that which is necessary and all other traffic is specifically denied
Outbound traffic from the CDE is restricted to only that which is necessary and all other traffic is specifically denied
NSCs are implemented between trusted and untrusted networks

name: Wireless Network Controls
description: Restrict and secure all wireless access to the cardholder data environment, including changing vendor defaults and using strong encryption

library_measure_controls.control_name: An accurate network diagram is maintained that shows all connections between the CDE and other networks, including any wireless networks
Wireless environments connected to the CDE or transmitting account data - all wireless vendor defaults are changed at installation

name: Secure System Defaults and Hardening
description: Change all vendor-supplied default passwords and remove or disable unnecessary default accounts, services, and protocols before deploying systems into production

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 2 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Configuration standards are developed, implemented, and maintained for all system components
Vendor default accounts are managed - default passwords changed, unnecessary default accounts removed or disabled

name: System Hardening Standards
description: Develop and apply configuration standards for all system components that address known security vulnerabilities and are consistent with industry-accepted hardening standards

library_measure_controls.control_name: Primary functions requiring different security levels are managed to ensure only one primary function exists per server
Only necessary services, protocols, daemons, and functions are enabled
All insecure services, protocols, or daemons are secured with appropriate security features
System security parameters are configured to prevent misuse

name: Stored Cardholder Data Protection
description: Protect stored account data through encryption, truncation, masking, or hashing, and minimize data storage amount and retention time

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 3 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Account data storage is kept to a minimum through data retention and disposal policies, procedures, and processes
SAD (Sensitive Authentication Data) is not stored after authorization, even if encrypted
SAD that is stored electronically prior to completion of authorization is encrypted using strong cryptography

name: PAN Display and Storage Restrictions
description: Render PAN unreadable anywhere it is stored and mask PAN when displayed so that only authorized personnel can see the full PAN

library_measure_controls.control_name: PAN is masked when displayed, with only personnel with a legitimate business need able to see more than the BIN and last four digits
PAN is rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored by using strong cryptography
Hashes used to render PAN unreadable are keyed cryptographic hashes of the entire PAN

name: Cryptographic Key Management
description: Implement proper cryptographic key management procedures including key generation, distribution, storage, rotation, and destruction

library_measure_controls.control_name: Procedures are defined and implemented to protect cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data against disclosure and misuse
Additional requirement for service providers: A documented description of the cryptographic architecture is maintained
Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include generation of strong cryptographic keys
Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include secure key distribution
Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include secure key storage
Key-management policies and procedures include cryptographic key changes for keys that have reached the end of their cryptoperiod
Key-management policies and procedures include the retirement, replacement, or destruction of keys as deemed necessary
Where manual cleartext cryptographic key-management operations are performed, key-management policies and procedures include split knowledge and dual control

name: Encryption of Data in Transit
description: Encrypt transmission of cardholder data across open, public networks using strong cryptography and security protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2+)

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 4 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Strong cryptography and security protocols are implemented to safeguard PAN during transmission over open, public networks
An inventory of the entity's trusted keys and certificates is maintained
PAN is secured with strong cryptography whenever it is sent via end-user messaging technologies

name: Anti-Malware Protection
description: Deploy and maintain anti-malware solutions on all systems commonly affected by malware, with regular updates and periodic scans

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 5 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
An anti-malware solution is deployed on all system components, except for those that are not commonly affected by malware
The deployed anti-malware solution detects all known types of malware and removes, blocks, or contains all known types of malware
Any system components that are not at risk for malware are evaluated periodically with a targeted risk analysis

name: Anti-Malware Maintenance and Monitoring
description: Ensure anti-malware mechanisms are kept current, perform periodic scans, generate audit logs, and cannot be disabled or altered by users without authorization

library_measure_controls.control_name: The anti-malware solution is kept current via automatic updates
The anti-malware solution performs periodic scans and active or real-time scans, or performs continuous behavioral analysis of systems or processes
For removable electronic media, the anti-malware solution performs automatic scans or continuous behavioral analysis when media is inserted, connected, or logically mounted
Audit logs for the anti-malware solution are enabled and retained
Anti-malware mechanisms cannot be disabled or altered by users, unless specifically documented and authorized by management on a case-by-case basis

name: Phishing and Social Engineering Controls
description: Implement mechanisms to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks, including email filtering, awareness training, and reporting processes

library_measure_controls.control_name: Processes and automated mechanisms are in place to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks

name: Secure Software Development Lifecycle
description: Develop and maintain secure systems and software by following a secure software development lifecycle, including secure coding practices and code reviews

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 6 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Bespoke and custom software are developed securely, including software development processes based on industry standards and/or best practices
Software development personnel working on bespoke and custom software are trained at least once every 12 months on software security relevant to their job function
Bespoke and custom software is reviewed prior to being released into production or to customers, to identify and correct potential coding vulnerabilities
Software engineering techniques or other methods are defined and in use by software development personnel to prevent or mitigate common software attacks

name: Vulnerability and Patch Management
description: Identify, prioritize, and address security vulnerabilities promptly. Install critical security patches within one month of release

library_measure_controls.control_name: Security vulnerabilities are identified and managed by installing applicable security patches/updates and performing code evaluations
An inventory of bespoke and custom software, and third-party software components incorporated into bespoke and custom software is maintained to facilitate vulnerability and patch management
All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches/updates within one month of release

name: Change Control Procedures
description: Implement change control processes for all changes to system components in the CDE, including documentation, impact analysis, approval, testing, and rollback procedures

library_measure_controls.control_name: Changes to all system components in the production environment are made according to established procedures that include documentation of impact, approval by authorized parties, functionality testing, and back-out procedures
Upon completion of a significant change, all applicable PCI DSS requirements are confirmed to be in place on all new or changed systems and networks, and documentation is updated as applicable
Pre-production environments are separated from production environments and the separation is enforced with access controls
Roles and functions are separated between production and pre-production environments
Live PANs are not used in pre-production environments, except where those environments are included in the CDE
Test data and test accounts are removed from system components before the system goes into production

name: Web Application Security
description: Protect public-facing web applications against attacks using WAFs, automated vulnerability assessments, or manual application security reviews

library_measure_controls.control_name: For public-facing web applications, new threats and vulnerabilities are addressed on an ongoing basis and applications are protected against known attacks
For public-facing web applications, an automated technical solution is deployed that continually detects and prevents web-based attacks
All payment page scripts that are loaded and executed in the consumer's browser are managed - an inventory is maintained, authorization is confirmed, integrity is assured

name: User Identification and Authentication
description: Assign a unique identification to each person with computer access and implement strong authentication mechanisms to ensure proper identity verification

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 7 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 8 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
All users are assigned a unique ID before access to system components or cardholder data is allowed
Group, shared, or generic accounts, or other shared authentication credentials are only used when necessary on an exception basis

name: Role-Based Access Control
description: Restrict access to system components and cardholder data to only those individuals whose job requires such access, using role-based access control (RBAC) and least privilege principles

library_measure_controls.control_name: An access control model is defined and includes granting access based on the entity's business and access needs
Access is assigned to users, including privileged users, based on job classification and function
Required privileges are approved by authorized personnel
All user accounts and related access privileges, including third-party/vendor accounts, are reviewed at least once every six months
All application and system accounts and related access privileges are assigned and managed based on least privilege

name: Strong Password and Authentication Policies
description: Enforce strong password/authentication policies including minimum length (12+ characters), complexity requirements, password history, and account lockout mechanisms

library_measure_controls.control_name: All user access to system components for users and administrators is authenticated via at least one authentication factor
Invalid authentication attempts are limited by locking out the user ID after not more than 10 attempts
If passwords/passphrases are used as authentication factors, they meet a minimum level of complexity of at least 12 characters containing both numeric and alphabetic characters
Individuals are not allowed to submit a new password/passphrase that is the same as any of the last four passwords/passphrases used
If passwords/passphrases are used as the only authentication factor for user access, passwords/passphrases are either changed at least once every 90 days, or dynamically analyzed for security

name: Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all access into the CDE, for all remote network access, and for all non-console administrative access

library_measure_controls.control_name: MFA is implemented for all non-console access into the CDE for personnel with administrative access
MFA is implemented for all access into the CDE
MFA is implemented for all remote network access originating from outside the entity's network that could access or impact the CDE
MFA systems are implemented so that they cannot be bypassed by any users, including administrative users

name: Session Timeout and Idle Controls
description: Configure system/session idle timeout to 15 minutes or less and require re-authentication to reactivate the terminal or session

library_measure_controls.control_name: If a user session has been idle for more than 15 minutes, the user is required to re-authenticate to re-activate the terminal or session

name: Service and Application Account Management
description: Manage application and system accounts, including interactive login controls, password rotation, and restricting usage to the minimum necessary

library_measure_controls.control_name: If accounts used by systems or applications can be used for interactive login, they are managed as follows: interactive use is prevented unless needed for an exceptional circumstance, and additional scrutiny is applied
Passwords/passphrases for any application and system accounts that can be used for interactive login are not hard coded in scripts, configuration/property files, or bespoke and custom source code
Passwords/passphrases for any application and system accounts are protected against misuse

name: Physical Access Controls
description: Restrict and monitor physical access to systems in the cardholder data environment using access control mechanisms such as badges, locks, and video surveillance

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 9 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Appropriate facility entry controls are in place to restrict physical access to systems in the CDE
Physical and/or logical controls are implemented to restrict use of publicly accessible network jacks within the facility
Physical access to wireless access points, gateways, networking/communications hardware, and telecommunication lines within the facility is restricted
Access to consoles in sensitive areas is restricted via locking when not in use

name: Visitor Management
description: Implement procedures to identify, authorize, and manage visitors in areas where cardholder data is present, including visitor logs and escort requirements

library_measure_controls.control_name: Procedures are implemented for authorizing and managing physical access of personnel to the CDE, including identifying personnel and visitors, managing changes to requirements, and revoking or terminating access immediately
Procedures are implemented for authorizing and managing visitor access to the CDE
Visitor badges or identification are surrendered or deactivated before visitors leave the facility or at the date of expiration

A visitor log is used to maintain a physical record of visitor activity in the facility as well as in sensitive areas, including the visitor's name, firm, and the onsite personnel authorizing physical access

name: Media Protection and Disposal
description: Protect all media containing cardholder data, implement secure media distribution procedures, and destroy media when it is no longer needed

library_measure_controls.control_name: All media with cardholder data is physically secured
All media with cardholder data is classified in accordance with the sensitivity of the data
Media with cardholder data sent outside the facility is secured via tracked delivery, with management approval prior to moving
Inventory logs of all electronic media with cardholder data are maintained
Hard-copy materials with cardholder data are destroyed when no longer needed for business or legal reasons
Electronic media with cardholder data is destroyed when no longer needed for business or legal reasons

name: Point-of-Interaction Device Protection
description: Protect point-of-interaction (POI) devices from tampering and unauthorized substitution by maintaining a device inventory and periodic inspections

library_measure_controls.control_name: POI devices that capture payment card data via direct physical interaction with the payment card form factor are protected from tampering and unauthorized substitution
An up-to-date list of POI devices is maintained, including make, model, location, and device serial number
POI device surfaces are periodically inspected to detect tampering and unauthorized substitution
Training is provided for personnel in POI environments to be aware of attempted tampering or replacement of POI devices

name: Audit Logging and Monitoring
description: Implement audit trails and logging to link all access to system components to individual users, recording user activities, exceptions, faults, and information security events

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 10 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Audit logs are enabled and active for all system components and cardholder data
Audit logs capture all individual user access to cardholder data
Audit logs capture all actions taken by any individual with administrative access
Audit logs capture all access to audit logs
Audit logs capture all invalid logical access attempts
Audit logs capture all changes to identification and authentication credentials
Audit logs capture initialization of new audit logs, stopping or pausing of existing audit logs
Audit logs capture creation and deletion of system-level objects

name: Audit Log Content and Protection
description: Record sufficient detail in audit log entries and protect audit trails from unauthorized modification using time synchronization and access controls

library_measure_controls.control_name: Audit logs record sufficient detail for each auditable event: user identification, type of event, date and time, success or failure, origination of event, identity or name of affected data, system component, resource, or service
Read access to audit logs files is limited to those with a job-related need
Audit log files are protected to prevent modifications by individuals
Audit log files, including for external-facing technologies, are promptly backed up to a secure, central, internal log server(s) or other media that is difficult to alter
File integrity monitoring or change-detection mechanisms is used on audit logs to ensure that existing log data cannot be changed without generating alerts
System clocks and time are synchronized using time-synchronization technology
Systems are configured to the correct and consistent time as: one or more designated time servers are in use, and only the designated central time servers receive time from external sources
Time synchronization settings and data are protected: access to time data is restricted, and changes to time settings on critical systems are logged, monitored, and reviewed

name: Log Retention
description: Retain audit log history for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months immediately available for analysis

library_measure_controls.control_name: Retain audit log history for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months immediately available for analysis

name: Security Event Detection and Response
description: Implement automated mechanisms to perform audit log reviews and alert personnel of suspected or confirmed security events, including anomalies and indicators of compromise

library_measure_controls.control_name: Audit logs are reviewed at least once daily to identify anomalies or suspicious activity
Automated mechanisms are used to perform audit log reviews
Logs of all other system components are reviewed periodically based on the entity's policies and risk management strategy
Exceptions and anomalies identified during the review process are addressed
Additional requirement for service providers: Failures of critical security control systems are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly

name: Vulnerability Scanning
description: Perform internal and external network vulnerability scans at least quarterly and after significant changes, with external scans performed by an ASV

library_measure_controls.control_name: All security policies and operational procedures identified in Requirement 11 are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties
Internal vulnerability scans are performed at least once every three months
All other applicable vulnerabilities found during internal vulnerability scans are managed per the entity's targeted risk analysis
External vulnerability scans are performed at least once every three months by a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV)

name: Penetration Testing
description: Perform internal and external penetration testing at least annually and after significant infrastructure or application changes

library_measure_controls.control_name: External penetration testing is performed at least once every 12 months and after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade or change
Internal penetration testing is performed at least once every 12 months and after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade or change
Exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses found during penetration testing are corrected per the entity's assessment of risk

If segmentation is used to isolate the CDE from other networks, penetration tests are performed on segmentation controls at least once every 12 months and after any changes to segmentation controls/methods

name: Wireless Access Point Detection
description: Detect and identify authorized and unauthorized wireless access points on a quarterly basis using wireless analyzers, NAC, or IDS/IPS

library_measure_controls.control_name: Authorized and unauthorized wireless access points are managed by testing for the presence of wireless (Wi-Fi) access points and detecting and identifying all authorized and unauthorized wireless access points on a quarterly basis
An inventory of authorized wireless access points is maintained, including a documented business justification

name: Intrusion Detection and File Integrity Monitoring
description: Deploy intrusion-detection and/or intrusion-prevention techniques on the network and file integrity monitoring on critical system files

library_measure_controls.control_name: Intrusion-detection and/or intrusion-prevention techniques are used to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the network
Intrusion-detection and/or intrusion-prevention techniques detect, alert on/prevent, and address covert malware communication channels
A change-detection mechanism (file integrity monitoring) is deployed to alert personnel to unauthorized modification of critical system files, configuration files, or content files

name: Unauthorized Change Detection on Payment Pages
description: Deploy a mechanism to detect and alert on unauthorized modifications to HTTP headers and the contents of payment pages as received by the consumer browser

library_measure_controls.control_name: A change- and tamper-detection mechanism is deployed to alert personnel to unauthorized modification to the HTTP headers and the contents of payment pages as received by the consumer browser

name: Information Security Policy
description: Establish, publish, maintain, and disseminate a comprehensive information security policy that addresses all PCI DSS requirements and is reviewed at least annually

library_measure_controls.control_name: An overall information security policy is established, published, maintained, and disseminated to all relevant personnel, as well as to relevant vendors and business partners
The information security policy is reviewed at least once every 12 months and updated as needed to reflect changes to business objectives or the risk environment
The security policy clearly defines information security roles and responsibilities for all personnel

name: Acceptable Use Policies
description: Develop and implement acceptable use policies for end-user technologies, including explicit approval requirements, acceptable uses, and approved products/locations

library_measure_controls.control_name: Responsibility for information security is formally assigned to a Chief Information Security Officer or other information security knowledgeable member of senior management
Acceptable use policies for end-user technologies are documented and implemented

name: Risk Assessment Program
description: Implement a formal risk assessment process performed at least annually and upon significant changes that identifies critical assets, threats, and vulnerabilities

library_measure_controls.control_name: Each PCI DSS requirement that provides flexibility for how frequently it is performed is supported by a targeted risk analysis
A targeted risk analysis is performed for each PCI DSS requirement that the entity meets with the customized approach
Cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use are documented and reviewed at least once every 12 months
Hardware and software technologies in use are reviewed at least once every 12 months to confirm they continue to receive security fixes from vendors

name: PCI DSS Scope Documentation
description: Document and confirm PCI DSS scope at least annually and upon significant changes, including all data flows, system components, and network connections

library_measure_controls.control_name: An inventory of system components that are in scope for PCI DSS, including a description of function/use, is maintained and kept current
PCI DSS scope is documented and confirmed by the entity at least once every 12 months and upon significant change to the in-scope environment
Additional requirement for service providers: significant changes to organizational structure result in a documented review of the impact to PCI DSS scope and applicability of controls

name: Security Awareness Training
description: Implement a formal security awareness program for all personnel, including upon hire and at least annually, covering threats, cardholder data handling, and incident response

library_measure_controls.control_name: A formal security awareness program is implemented to make all personnel aware of the entity's information security policy and procedures
The security awareness program is reviewed at least once every 12 months and updated as needed
Personnel receive security awareness training upon hire and at least once every 12 months
Security awareness training includes awareness of threats and vulnerabilities that could impact the security of account data
Security awareness training includes awareness about the acceptable use of end-user technologies

name: Personnel Screening
description: Screen potential personnel prior to hire to minimize the risk of internal attacks, including background checks within legal constraints

library_measure_controls.control_name: Potential personnel who will have access to the CDE are screened, within the constraints of local laws, prior to hire

name: Third-Party Service Provider Management
description: Maintain policies and procedures to manage third-party service providers (TPSPs) with whom account data is shared or that could affect the security of account data

library_measure_controls.control_name: A list of all third-party service providers (TPSPs) with which account data is shared or that could affect the security of account data is maintained
Written agreements with TPSPs are maintained that include acknowledgements from TPSPs that they are responsible for the security of account data they possess
An established process is implemented for engaging TPSPs, including proper due diligence prior to engagement
A program is implemented to monitor TPSPs' PCI DSS compliance status at least once every 12 months
Information is maintained about which PCI DSS requirements are managed by each TPSP, which are managed by the entity, and any that are shared between both the TPSP and the entity

name: Incident Response Plan
description: Establish, document, and distribute an incident response plan to be initiated immediately upon suspected or confirmed security breach, including roles, communication, and recovery procedures

library_measure_controls.control_name: An incident response plan exists and is ready to be activated in the event of a suspected or confirmed security incident
At least once every 12 months, the security incident response plan is reviewed and the content is updated as needed
Specific personnel are designated to be available on a 24/7 basis to respond to suspected or confirmed security incidents
Personnel responsible for responding to suspected and confirmed security incidents are appropriately and periodically trained
The frequency of periodic training for incident response personnel is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis
The security incident response plan includes monitoring and responding to alerts from security monitoring systems including IDS/IPS, network security controls, FIM, and anti-malware
The security incident response plan is modified and evolved according to lessons learned and to incorporate industry developments
Incident response procedures are in place, to be initiated upon the detection of stored PAN anywhere it is not expected
